topic: Christmas cooking marathon: back care in the kitchen

slides.headline: Cooking for twelve this Christmas?
slides.sub: Long hours at the bench add up. A few kitchen tweaks help.

slides.title: Bring the job up to you
slides.body: Benches suit some heights better than others. For long chopping jobs, a thick board raises the work, or sit at the table for peeling and prepping so your back gets a break.

slides.title: Stagger your stance
slides.body: Standing square to the bench for an hour loads the same tissues nonstop. Rest one foot on a low step or open cupboard shelf, and swap sides every few minutes.

slides.title: Lift the roast with a plan
slides.body: Heavy trays come out of low ovens. Squat down close, keep the tray near your body and turn with your feet, not your spine. Grab a helper for the big ones.

slides.title: Break the marathon into rounds
slides.body: Prep in 20 to 30 minute rounds. Between them, walk the hallway, do a few standing back bends or sit for a minute. Small breaks usually beat one long rest at the end.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Back pain that spreads down a leg, numbness, pain that wakes you and won't ease, or a sudden flare-up that isn't settling after a few days is worth an assessment.

slides.headline: Back sore after the big cook?
slides.body: Our chiropractors look at how you move and load your back, using hands-on care alongside simple exercises. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Cooking for twelve this Christmas? Your back might feel it before the pudding comes out.

Long stretches at the bench, low ovens and heavy roasting trays are a lot of load in one day. It's rarely one lift that does it. More often it's hours in the same position.

A few tweaks help: raise the work or sit to prep, stagger your stance, lift trays close to your body and turn with your feet, and cook in rounds with short breaks in between.

If your back is grumbling after the festive cook, our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy can help with hands-on care plus exercises. Book online via the link in bio. 🎄

story.headline: Long day at the bench?
story.body: Rest one foot on a low shelf, swap every few minutes, and take a short walk every half hour.
